sources.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
sources.locator: Complete 7-page paper; §1, equations (1)–(4), PDF pp. 1–2; Lemma 1 and its complete bias–variance and one-coordinate maximizer proof, PDF pp. 2–3; Definitions 3–5 and operator/statistical ill-posedness distinction, PDF p. 5.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 7-page PDF. Read the full operator-to-sequence reduction, kernel-orthogonality qualification, ellipsoid definition, cutoff definition, complete Lemma 1 risk proof, and the later taxonomy distinguishing polynomially decaying (moderately ill-posed) operators from exponentially decaying (severely ill-posed) operators and statistical minimax-rate terminology.

contents.name: Compact inverse white-noise model and SVD sequence coordinates
contents.support: Supports the observation model y^sigma=Tx+sigma xi, normalized sequence observations theta_j+sigma s_j^{-1}xi_j, the positive singular-value convention, and the required truth restriction x in N(T)^perp. The local model gives the full measurable pushforward and zero-noise boundary.

contents.name: Weighted ellipsoid class
contents.support: Supports Theta_a(Q) with positive increasing weights and finite radius; the local definition states the nondecreasing convention and explicitly does not assume compactness.

contents.name: Cutoff procedure and exact heteroscedastic risk
contents.locator: equation (11), Lemma 1 and complete proof, PDF pp. 2–3
contents.support: Supports retaining the first D normalized coordinates and zeroing the rest.

contents.name: Exact bias–variance formula and one-coordinate tail attainer
contents.support: Supports the retained-coordinate variance sum, monotone-weight tail bound, and equality at a truth supported only on D+1; the local proof supplies all details independently.

contents.name: Polynomial and exponential singular-value regimes
contents.support: Supports the operator taxonomy: polynomial singular decay is moderately ill-posed, while exponential decay is severely ill-posed. The design’s word mildly is not used for the polynomial operator regime.

contents.name: Exponential singular-value regime
contents.support: Supports the exponentially decaying operator convention; the local example substitutes an exact exponential sequence into the proven risk identity.

contents.name: Zero-noise endpoint
contents.locator: No zero-noise theorem is asserted in this source; the paper assumes sigma>0.
contents.support: Ding–Mathé assumes positive noise and makes no zero-noise assertion. The local exact-risk proof separately defines and proves the epsilon=0 deterministic boundary, so no zero-noise claim is imported from this source.

sources.title: Iain M. Johnstone, Gaussian estimation: Sequence and wavelet models, draft version December 27, 2011
sources.locator: Complete 446-page manuscript; §3.1, sequence sample space, squared ell2 risk and ellipsoid equation (3.4), printed pp. 56–59 / PDF pp. 71–75; §3.2, equations (3.11)–(3.12) and full cutoff-tail maximizer argument, printed pp. 60–61 / PDF pp. 75–77; §3.8, equations (3.63)–(3.67), printed pp. 77–79 / PDF pp. 92–94.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched the complete 446-page manuscript and read all cited passages. Section 3.1 gives the product-sequence Gaussian model, ell2 squared-error risk and ellipsoid convention. Section 3.2 derives the coordinatewise variance–bias decomposition and the first-omitted-axis maximizer for the homoscedastic special case. Section 3.8 derives the compact-SVD inverse sequence model and inverse-singular-value noise amplification. Section 3.8 writes the signal expansion first for the injective case; the present model explicitly uses only minimum-norm coordinates in N(K)^perp, consistent with Ding–Mathé and the local SVD suppliers.

contents.name: Sequence experiment and product sample space
contents.support: Independent book treatment of the countable Gaussian sequence sample space and the l2 parameter convention.

contents.name: Ellipsoids and squared sequence loss
contents.support: Independent weighted-ellipsoid convention; the local definition fixes nondecreasing positive weights and states that compactness is not assumed.

contents.name: Singular-value coordinates for inverse white noise
contents.support: Independent SVD-coordinate conversion from functional white noise to observations with noise scaled by the inverse singular values.

contents.name: Cutoff estimator risk and tail maximizer
contents.support: Independent derivation of the variance–bias decomposition and extremizing first omitted axis when the weights are nondecreasing; the book treats equal coordinate variances, while Ding–Mathé and the local proof cover inverse-problem heteroscedasticity.

sources.title: Christian Clason, Introduction to Finite Element Methods, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1709.08618v2
sources.locator: Complete 118-page lecture notes; Chapter 12 “Galerkin approach for parabolic problems,” §§29–30, printed/PDF pp. 102–110.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched the full 118-page notes and read Chapter 12, including §29 “Galerkin methods,” Theorems 12.1–12.2, §30 “A priori error estimates,” and Theorems 12.3–12.4. These concern discontinuous-Galerkin existence/stability and parabolic finite-element error estimates; the complete chapter has no white-noise, variance, or statistical-risk treatment. This is the identifiable Clason Chapter 12 citation in current repository plan evidence, but it cannot support the IP-08 white-noise risk claims.

contents.name: §29 Galerkin methods
contents.reason: This section develops conforming and discontinuous Galerkin discretizations for parabolic PDEs, not a Gaussian observation model or statistical inverse-risk calculation.

contents.name: Theorem 12.1
contents.reason: This theorem establishes existence and uniqueness for a finite-dimensional discontinuous-Galerkin parabolic problem, not a Gaussian sequence estimator or its statistical risk.

contents.name: Theorem 12.2
contents.reason: This theorem is a stability estimate for a discontinuous-Galerkin approximation of a parabolic PDE and does not address white noise, inverse singular values, or expected risk.

contents.name: §30 A priori error estimates
contents.reason: This section estimates temporal and spatial discretization errors for parabolic finite elements, a deterministic approximation topic outside the Gaussian sequence-risk claims.

contents.name: Theorem 12.3
contents.reason: This theorem bounds a parabolic finite-element solution error for the degree-zero discontinuous-Galerkin case; it is not a statistical white-noise risk result.

contents.name: Theorem 12.4
contents.reason: This theorem bounds a parabolic finite-element solution error for the degree-one discontinuous-Galerkin case; it is not a Gaussian sequence or inverse-problem risk result.
